plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Reduce CRWD to 10% to manage single name risk.
Buy MRVL at 5% to add a high-scoring, quality name.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, aiming for lower drawdowns. Risk is managed through diversification and quality names.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Reduce SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Trim CRWD to 10% to manage single name risk.
Buy MRVL at 4% to add a high-scoring tech name.
This plan balances growth with risk management.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It maintains some exposure to leveraged ETFs while reducing overall concentration. Expect moderate drawdowns with a blend of broad index and quality tech.

plan: Add to SOXL and SPAL, targeting 6% each, to increase leveraged exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Maintain CRWD at 14% to press a working position.
Buy MRVL at 6% to add a high-scoring setup.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for stretch growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of higher potential drawdowns and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETFs.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to increase income exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Sell CRWD and SMH to zero to reduce high-beta single names.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth, rotating into income and broad index ETFs. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
